💡 The novelty lies in using interlayer electronic coupling with adjacent Co single atoms and nanoparticles to tune FePc's spin state and frontier orbitals. This suppresses Fe 3d spin polarization and enhances dz2 electron localization, optimizing intermediate adsorption. The strategy yields high ORR activity (0.927 V half-wave potential, 336 mW cm–2 peak power) and durability, offering a general approach for engineering molecular Fe–N4 electrocatalysts.

item.description:

Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in solvent/anion codepleted solvation engineering using TMSB to competitively complex PF6–, creating low-coordination electrolytes that boost conductivity and lower desolvation barriers. This enables high-voltage, low-temperature sodium-ion batteries, achieving 200 Wh kg–1 in a 6.8 Ah pouch cell and 162 Wh kg–1 at −20 °C—a generalizable paradigm for extreme-environment energy storage.
🏷 sodium-ion battery · low-coordination electrolyte · solvation engineering · low-temperature operation · pouch cell

item.title: Breaking the “Micro-Size Inversion” Paradox via a Surface-Chemistry-Driven Molecular Sieving Membrane for Ambient Lithium–Air Batteries
item.description:

Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a surface-chemistry-driven sieving membrane (PDMS/COF-VF) that overcomes the size-inversion paradox by using hydrogen-bond-repellent perfluoroalkyl grafts to block polar H2O while allowing nonpolar O2 transport. Its significance: enabling ambient lithium–air batteries with 3596 mAh g–1 capacity and 2700 h cycling (10.8-fold improvement), suppressing LiOH formation and advancing practical energy storage.

This enables tunable pore size and wrinkle degree, and as a sodium storage anode delivers high rate capability and long cyclability, offering an effective route to ultrafast mesopore highways.
